distinguishing_fact: Subheading 5205.12.2000 covers bleached, dyed, or mercerized yarns. CBP laboratory analysis confirmed both samples are unbleached and not mercerized, directing classification specifically to 5205.12.1000.
reasoning: The merchandise consists of 100% cotton, 1-ply (single) yarns made of carded open-end spun (uncombed) cotton fibers. Under Note 4 to Section XI, because the samples with support weigh 1,126 g and 516 g (exceeding 125 g), the yarns are not put up for retail sale and classify in heading 5205. The metric counts are 20.1 Nm and 27.03 Nm, which fall in the range exceeding 14 Nm but not exceeding 43 Nm under subheading 5205.12. Because laboratory analysis established that both yarns are unbleached and not mercerized, they classify in 8-digit tariff line 5205.12.1000.

citations.quote: The applicable subheading for the 100 percent cotton carded open end single yarn, unbleached, not mercerized, measuring 16.9 Nm will be 5205.12.1000, HTSUS

The applicable subheading for the cotton yarn will be 5205.12.1000, Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTS), which provides for cotton yarn (other than sewing thread), containing 85 percent or more by weight of cotton, not put up for retail sale: single yarn, of uncombed fibers: exceeding 14 nm but not exceeding 43 nm: unbleached, not mercerized.

distinguishing_fact: Subheading 8424.41.9000 encompasses small self-contained sprayers having a capacity not over 20 liters, whereas the FXS8/680 has a 600-liter capacity and is tractor-mounted/powered, classifying it under 8424.41.1000.
reasoning: The FXS8/680 is a horticultural sprayer equipped with a 600-liter tank, diaphragm pump, and 10 nozzles, designed to be mounted on a tractor via three hitch points and powered by the tractor to disperse pesticides and fertilizers over a 10-meter range. By application of GRI 1, the merchandise is classified under heading 8424 as a mechanical appliance for spraying or dispersing liquids. Correlation candidates in headings 8524, 8529, and 8549 are sweep headings for flat panel displays and electrical waste/scrap, which are excluded by Section XVI Note 6(A) and the physical nature of the functional, new sprayer. Pursuant to GRI 6, under subheading 8424.41 ('Portable sprayers'), the sprayer falls under 8-digit line 8424.41.1000 ('Sprayers (except sprayers, self-contained, having a capacity not over 20 liters)') because its 600-liter capacity far exceeds 20 liters.

citations.quote: Throughout the tariff schedule, “electrical and electronic waste and scrap” means electrical and electronic assemblies, printed circuit boards, and electrical or electronic articles that: (a) have been rendered unusable for their original purposes by breakage, cutting-up or other processes or are economically unsuitable for repair, refurbishment or renovation to render them fit for their original purposes

distinguishing_fact: The merchandise is a newly manufactured, fully functioning rechargeable lithium-ion battery. Heading 8549 covers spent accumulators and electrical waste/scrap, whereas functional electric storage batteries are classified in heading 8507.
reasoning: The item is a functional prismatic lithium-ion storage battery (accumulator) comprising two rechargeable lithium-ion cells welded in series within an aluminum housing. Under GRI 1 and Note 3 to Chapter 85, electric accumulators/storage batteries with protective housings and electrical contacts are classifiable in heading 8507. Subheading 8507.60 directly provides for 'Lithium-ion batteries' at the 8-digit level (8507.60.00). The candidate sweep subheadings under heading 8549 cover electrical waste, scrap, and spent accumulators (defined in Subheading Note 5 to Chapter 85 as those neither usable nor capable of being recharged), which explicitly excludes new, functional rechargeable batteries.

citations.quote: For the purposes of heading 8507, the expression "electric accumulators" includes those presented with ancillary components which contribute to the accumulator's function of storing and supplying energy or protect it from damage, such as electrical connectors, temperature control devices (for example, thermistors) and circuit protection devices. They may also include a portion of the protective housing of the goods in which they are to be used.

For the purposes of subheadings 8549.11 to 8549.19, “spent primary cells, spent primary batteries and spent electric accumulators: are those which are neither usable as such because of breakage, cutting-up, wear or other reasons, nor capable of being recharged.
